newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ seen keeping easy credit policy in 1997 - Daiwa.
newsitem.headline: BOJ seen keeping easy credit policy in 1997 - Daiwa.

text.p: The head of the bond department at Japan's second-largest brokerage said on Monday the likelihood of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) abandoning its current easy credit policy before the beginning of autumn 1997 was very slim.

Akira Kiyota, director of the bond and finance division at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd, told reporters that the central bank is more likely to hold interest rates steady through 1997, possibly until the spring of 1998, as it needed to wait until the summer of 1997 to start assessing the impact of a planned consumption tax hike in April 1997.
Japan's official discount rate (ODR) has been at a record low of 0.5 percent since September 1995.

Kiyota said the combination of a consumption tax hike to five percent from three percent, and the likely government decision to discontinue special income tax cuts in 1997 could add up to a tax increase of about seven trillion yen in the fiscal year that starts in April 1997, an unprecedented amount for a single fiscal year.
"With major deflationary factors in the pipeline, it is highly doubtful that the BOJ can actually raise interest rates," Kiyota said.

Kiyota said he expects the likely continuation of the BOJ's easy credit policy and the expected inflow of public funds into bonds to help support the Japanese government bond (JGB) market in coming months.

The bulk of the money from the funds, which were set up as part of a government scheme to resolve the problem loans of failed mortgage firms or "jusen", is expected to be eventually invested in JGBs, market experts say.
Also, the BOJ and the Finance Ministry's Trust Fund Bureau are expected to continue their outright purchases of JGBs, Kiyota said.

Daiwa forecasts the yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB will move in a range of 2.35 to 2.90 percent in the October-December quarter of 1996, and between 2.50 and 3.00 percent in the January-March quarter of 1997.
The yield of the 182nd JGB ended Tokyo trade at 2.750 percent on Monday.
